answer: Behavioral Vertex Clustering. Each identity is plotted as a vertex in a transaction graph; genuine agents form dense islands of repeated counterparties, while sybils branch thinly. A retrospective scan flags clusters whose internal edge overlap falls below the cohort median across a rolling tide of activity windows. Flagged clusters lose settlement priority, forcing attackers to fabricate sustained reciprocal trade per clone—costing roughly one full agent-month of genuine-looking volume per identity to evade detection.
